oliver: Nightly eval threw a regression on long-context instruction prompts (pset-8242). Outputs are dropping the system/instruction prefix — looks like truncation mid-sentence for prompts >~6k tokens. Posting a clipped sample below.

jen: ack — which model / quant / runtime were used for the nightly run?

oliver: model=redwood-vicuna-13b-8k, quant=q4_0, runtime=runtime-v2.11.3. eval-bot summary attached to the run.

eval-bot: nightly-run 2026-03-19T03:12:08Z - regression detected: 7/120 prompts failing on instruction-following at longctx; median BLEU down 0.18; examples bucketed under "incomplete_system".

oliver: Example (prompt id pset-8242/item-17):
```
SYSTEM: You are a helpful assistant. Follow these instructions exactly: give step-by-step reasoning, end with a short summary.
USER: [very long context ~5.5k tokens omitted]
ASSISTANT: Sure, here's how I would approach this...
...
<generated output starts mid-instruction> "end with a short"
```
The generation literally starts in the middle of the system sentence. So the model output lacks the beginning of the instruction.

chris: :thinking_face: we recently landed a change to KV offset arithmetic (runtime commit abc12345) that touched wrap/overflow handling for long sequences. Could be an indexing regression on continuous KV reuse.

maya: Good call. I'll run the reproducer with kv debug logs. Use REDWOOD_KV_DEBUG=1 and set sequence len to 8192. Command I'm using: 
```
REDWOOD_KV_DEBUG=1 python tools/repro_longctx.py --model redwood-vicuna-13b --quant q4_0 --seq 8192 --prompt-id pset-8242/item-17 --no-cache=false
```
This will print KV offsets and eviction events.

sam: Also check tokenizer boundary behavior — if tokenization differs between eval harness and runtime (esp with whitespace/soft-BPE) it can shift token offsets and cause "lost instruction" symptoms. Any recent tokenizer changes?

luis: I'm assigning to myself for triage. Plan: 1) reproduce locally with the exact nightly container, 2) run with KVCACHE disabled (no caching) to see if issue disappears, 3) run against previous runtime tag (v2.11.2) to bisect, 4) collect KV offset logs and final token positions for failing items, 5) check for quantization path differences (q4_0 kernel variants). I'll post diffs and logs here.

deploy-bot: canary rollout runtime-v2.11.3 -> infra-hostpool-1 at 2026-03-18T22:41Z (includes commit abc12345).

jen: Thanks — very helpful. If disabling KVCACHE fixes it we should hotfix roll back kv index change ASAP. If not, we check tokenizer + quant path.

oliver: On it. Pushed a lightweight repro to my branch and started a local run — will post results in ~20m.

luis: ping me when you have logs. I'll prioritize the bisect. If we confirm it's runtime-related I'll open an incident and request a rollback.

chris: FYI I also saw a small bump in continuous batching code around the same timeframe; if KV offsets are computed per-batch it could interact. Will double-check my PRs.

maya: reproduced locally — I can reproduce the mid-instruction start when KVCACHE is enabled; when I run with --no-cache the output contains the full system instruction. Adding my logs to the run (kv_offset sequence shows a wrap at token idx ~6146).

sam: sounds like offset wrap. Could be 16-bit counter overflow or incorrect mod.

luis: OK that narrows it. I'll grab the runtime binary and run the v2.11.2 vs v2.11.3 diff and look specifically at KV index math. Will update in this thread.

oliver: Great triage so far — thanks @luis @maya. Posting follow-ups here. :thumbsup:
